original_value: Due to its all time capability, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) remote sensing plays an important role in Earth observation. The ability to interpret the data is limited, even for experts, as the human eye is not familiar to the impact of distance-dependent imaging, signal intensities detected in the radar spectrum as well as image characteristics related to speckle or steps of post-processing. This paper is concerned with machine learning for SAR-to-optical image-to-image translation in order to support the interpretation and analysis of original data. A conditional adversarial network is adopted and optimized in order to generate alternative SAR image representations based on the combination of SAR images (starting point) and optical images (reference) for training. Following this strategy, the focus is set on the value of empirical knowledge for initialization, the impact of results on follow-up applications, and the discussion of opportunities/drawbacks related to this application of deep learning. Case study results are shown for high resolution (SAR: TerraSAR-X, optical: ALOS PRISM) and low resolution (Sentinel-1 and -2) data. The properties of the alternative image representation are evaluated based on feedback from experts in SAR remote sensing and the impact on road extraction as an example for follow-up applications. The results provide the basis to explain fundamental limitations affecting the SAR-to-optical image translation idea but also indicate benefits from alternative SAR image representations.

result.paraphrase: Because of its all-weather, all-time capability, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) remote sensing is important for Earth observation. Yet even experts are limited in interpreting the data, since the human eye is not accustomed to distance-dependent imaging effects, signal intensities in the radar spectrum, or image traits introduced by speckle and post-processing. This paper addresses machine learning for SAR-to-optical image-to-image translation to improve interpretation and analysis of original data. A conditional adversarial network is used and optimized to generate alternative SAR image representations from SAR images as the starting point and optical images as reference data for training. In doing so, the study emphasizes the value of empirical knowledge for initialization, the effects on downstream applications, and the opportunities and drawbacks of this deep learning approach. Case studies are presented for high-resolution data (SAR: TerraSAR-X, optical: ALOS PRISM) and low-resolution data (Sentinel-1 and -2). The alternative image representation is assessed through feedback from SAR remote sensing experts and by its impact on road extraction as an example downstream task. The results help explain key limitations of the SAR-to-optical translation idea, while also showing the benefits of alternative SAR image representations.
